anti_overlap: fd-astar-correctness and fd-networkx-multigraph-routing own algorithmic and NetworkX-contract correctness — focus here on the shape of the Python surface humans/consumers see
fd-matplotlib-raster-basemap owns the PNG rendering — focus here on the library API the CLI consumes, not the PNG itself
decision_lens: Will every public name introduced here still be the right name when Phase 1.8 (GMaps comparator), the eventual frontend, and the app-layer persona binder all call it?
focus: Public Python API design for spatial.routing — function signatures, return tuples vs dataclasses, type hints, re-export surface, future-proofing.
name: fd-python-routing-api
persona: Apply the perspective of a Python library architect who builds platform-internal SDKs that survive 18-month refactors — they care about additive evolution, measure API surface against expected consumer count (frontend, CLI, app-layer persona binder, GMaps comparator), and flag any place where a return tuple, parameter name, or module export will force a breaking change in 1–2 sprints.
review_areas: Return type: 3-tuple (path, felt_minutes, walking_minutes) vs a RouteResult dataclass — the brainstorm itself lists 4 metrics in the GeoJSON properties (felt_minutes, walking_minutes, k, formula_id) suggesting the tuple will grow
Keyword-only weight parameter — is it a callable, a string ('felt_minutes'), or both? Consumers in Phase 1.8 will want to swap weights without re-implementing the callable
spatial/__init__.py re-export discipline — does adding astar/nearest_node/haversine_minutes alongside Phase 1.6's spatial.weights public surface create a flat namespace that collides later?
Type hints for graph (nx.MultiDiGraph specifically, not nx.Graph), node IDs (int vs Hashable), lat/lon (float vs a typed Coordinate)
CLI script ↔ library boundary — does route.py duplicate logic that should live in spatial.routing, or vice versa?
Versioning / formula_id propagation from FeltMinutesV0 through astar() to the GeoJSON properties (introduced as if free, but requires a contract)

severity_examples.condition: Adding fields to a positional tuple breaks every existing call site; a RouteResult dataclass would have been additive — choosing the tuple now creates a guaranteed breaking change in the next sprint
severity_examples.scenario: astar returns a 3-tuple now; Phase 1.8 needs (path, felt_minutes, walking_minutes, formula_id, shade_fraction)

severity_examples.condition: Phase 1.8 GMaps comparator wants weight='walking_minutes' to compare apples-to-apples — forced to build a trivial lambda wrapper every call site, then a follow-up sprint widens the type
severity_examples.scenario: weight parameter typed as Callable only

severity_examples.condition: OSMnx happens to return int OSM IDs today; if any future graph builder uses string IDs the type hint silently lies — small but real footgun
severity_examples.scenario: nearest_node returns int but graph node IDs are technically Hashable in NetworkX

success_hints: astar() returns a frozen dataclass (RouteResult) with at least path, felt_minutes, walking_minutes, formula_id; additive extension is documented
weight parameter accepts Callable | str with a registry for known names ('felt_minutes', 'walking_minutes')
Public surface in spatial/__init__.py is explicit (__all__) and module-scoped (spatial.routing.astar) is the recommended import
Type hints use nx.MultiDiGraph and a local Coordinate type alias; node IDs typed as int with a comment naming the OSMnx assumption
task_context: Reviewing a Phase 1.7 brainstorm that adds a new spatial.routing module (peer to spatial.weights) with three public functions and a CLI consumer. The module is platform-layer code expected to outlive Phase 1.7 and be called by the eventual frontend, the Phase 1.8 GMaps comparator, and app-layer persona binders. Review goal: catch API design choices that will force breaking changes in the next 1–3 sprints.
